Subject: Follow-up — additional transfer validation items

Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for the initial DPA annex you shared last week. Our legal and privacy teams ran a quick pass and have three follow-up asks so we can close the privacy section of our RFP: 

1) A mapping spreadsheet that ties each DPA annex clause to the applicable technical/organizational measures (we need specifics for "Transfers and safeguards" / Annex II equivalence points).
2) A current network diagram showing ingress/egress points for EU-origin traffic and any egress to non-EU regions.
3) The most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a short note on key management (do you use customer-managed KMS/HSM options or Redwood-managed keys today?).

We appreciate as much detail as you can provide; our timeline for review is tight (decision committee meets on 9/16). If helpful, we can take an hour with your security lead to walk through the diagram.

Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Head of Procurement, SentinelCare

P.S. please include a short note on how you treat partial pseudonymization for exported logs — that's a specific ask from our privacy counsel.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up — additional transfer validation items

Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the mapping workbook and a compact network diagram to this reply (see attachment stubs below). High-level answers to your three points are below; we can expand any item on the call.

1) DPA annex mapping: attached spreadsheet "redwood-dpa-annex-mapping-SentinelCare.xlsx" links each DPA clause to the implemented technical controls and the relevant documentation artifact (SOC2 section, infra runbook, audit logs). We align our transfers language to the latest EU SCCs and the EU-US Data Privacy Framework controls where applicable. For items that require additional contractual language (e.g., subprocessor obligations), we mark them in the workbook so legal can redline.

2) Network diagram: attached PDF shows ingress/egress flow for EU traffic. Summary: EU customer traffic is terminated in EU cloud regions by default; where workloads require fallbacks to US-hosted replicas we use TLS 1.3 for in-transit encryption and egress is through controlled NAT gateways with strict firewall ACLs. Drift from EU-only routing is logged and subject to automated alerts.

3) SOC 2 + KMS: attaching our SOC2 Type II (redacted for customer PII). Key management is Redwood-managed by default (Google Cloud KMS / AWS KMS depending on region) but we offer enterprise customers a customer-managed KMS integration or HSM-backed key wraps for private deployments. Note in the workbook which customers we have enabled CMK for in the past 12 months.

Regarding partial pseudonymization of logs: we redact end-user identifiers from non-essential logs by default and provide a configurable retention window; for exports we can provide a hashed identifier using a customer salt when requested (this is documented in the "log export" row of the mapping workbook).

Attachments: redwood-dpa-annex-mapping-SentinelCare.xlsx (workbook, mapping tabs), redwood-network-diagram-2026.pdf (PDF), SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2025.pdf (PDF).

If you want an hour slot, Marissa / Neha and I are available 9/14 or 9/15 morning ET — propose a 09:00 ET slot on 9/15 if that fits your committee prep.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Partner, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up — additional transfer validation items

Samir / Alicia — thanks, and appreciate the clear list. Short answers below — attaching a one-page supplement that you can drop into the RFP package (we also pushed the updated mapping workbook to the shared drive link).

• KMS / HSM availability: Customer-managed keys (CMK) are supported for both Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private deployments. For Redwood Hosted customers we offer a bring-your-own-KMS integration for enterprise contracts (we perform a key-wrapping flow so customer keys never leave their KMS; see the "Key Management" row in the supplement). HSM-backed key-protect (FIPS 140-2 L3) is available as an add-on for Dedicated and Private.

• Schrems II mitigations (summary paragraph): Redwood combines contractual safeguards (EU SCCs supplemented by a DPA annex that limits onward transfers and subprocessor use) with technical controls: data minimization and pseudonymization for exported artifacts, per-customer CMK/HSM options, region-aware routing with failover audit logs, and robust access controls (least privilege, just-in-time admin, and regular access reviews). We also enable TLS 1.3 for all transport, envelope encryption at rest, and provide customers with export logs and the ability to configure retention. When required, we will implement additional split-key or customer-secret-only unlock flows to reduce non-customer access surface.

• Subprocessor list: attached supplement includes the current encryption/logging subprocessors (cloud providers' managed key services and log ingestion tiers); we will provide an IP-protected appendix for contracting.

Next steps: we uploaded the supplement and the updated mapping workbook to the Drive link and can join your review call at 09:00 ET today if you'd like. If the committee needs anything else, flag it and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Compliance — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
